newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-HOLDERS PSG BEATEN 4-2 BY GALATASARAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HOLDERS PSG BEATEN 4-2 BY GALATASARAY.

text.p: Paris St Germain lost 4-2 to Galatasaray of Turkey on Thursday and have their work cut out if they are to defend their European Cup Winners' Cup title.

The Turks, inspired by Romanian international midfielder Gheorghe Hagi, took a 2-0 lead within the first 15 minutes of the second round first leg tie through striker Hakan Sukur and midfielder Tugay Kerimoglu.
But in an action-packed first half Galatasaray were then let down by goalkeeper Hayrettin Demirbas, who gifted the French league leaders two vital away goals within two minutes.

PSG captain Paul Le Guen scored with a speculative 35-metre shot that Demirbas allowed to creep inside his right-hand post, and then Brazilian Julio Cesar equalised with a looping header which the Turkish 'keeper could only fumble into his own net.
Sukur restored Galatasaray's lead with his second goal of the night just after the half hour, and Hakan Unsal gave the Turks a two-goal cushion shortly after the interval.
The home side dominated the second half and could have sewn up the tie with more goals, but the holders clung on and gave themselves hope for the second leg in Paris.
"It was pretty bad luck," Galatasaray captain Bulent Korkmaz said. "We gave away two easy goals."
